common.rconPasswordHelp: RCON is the remote-console protocol this panel uses to send commands to the running game — kicking players, saving the world, broadcasting messages, and everything else the panel does. This password is generated for you and the panel remembers it automatically. If you ever change it in the server's own settings later, update it here too, or the panel loses control of the server.
common.rconPortHelp: The port the panel uses to send RCON commands (start, stop, save, kick, chat) to the running server — separate from the port players connect on. Example: 27015 (the default). It must be free on this machine; if another program is already using it, the server may fail to start, or the panel may not be able to connect and control it.
common.ramHelp: Minimum is how much memory Project Zomboid reserves the moment it starts. Maximum is the hard ceiling it's allowed to grow to. Set Minimum too low and the server can stutter or crash once players and mods add up; set Maximum higher than the RAM this machine actually has and the server — or everything else running on it — can crash instead. Leave some headroom for the operating system.
common.gamePortHelp: The port Project Zomboid game clients connect to when players join. Example: 16261 (the default). If you change it, players must add the new number after your server address to connect (e.g. your-ip:16262), and your router or firewall must forward that same port instead.
common.adminPasswordHelp: Sets the password for Project Zomboid's built-in admin account. Once the server is running, use it in-game with the chat command /login admin, followed by this password, to get admin powers. Required before the first server start — the server can be installed without it, but won't start until one is set.
common.noSteamDesc: Use non-Steam mode (for GOG and LAN setups)
common.debugDesc: Enable verbose startup and runtime logs
common.customConfigLocationHelp: Project Zomboid normally stores saves, server config, and logs beside the install folder. Only set this if that data actually lives somewhere else — for example a separate drive, or a bind-mounted folder in Docker. Point this at the wrong folder and the panel won't find your existing saves, settings, or backups.
common.customDataPathPlaceholder: Path to the Zomboid data folder
common.noPermissionInstall: Installing a server requires the server.install permission, which this role doesn't have.
common.noPermissionSettings: Saving this setting requires the panel.settings permission, which this role doesn't have.
common.noPermissionControl: Starting the server requires the server.control permission, which this role doesn't have.

full.pageDescription: Download, configure, and register a new dedicated server.

step1.title: Set Up SteamCMD
step1.description: SteamCMD is required to download and update Project Zomboid dedicated server files.
step1.oneClickDesc: We will install SteamCMD and prepare it for this panel.
step1.pathPlaceholder: Select or enter the SteamCMD folder path
step1.manualTrigger: Already have SteamCMD? Set the folder manually
step1.manualStep2: Extract SteamCMD to a folder on the panel host.
step1.manualStep2Windows: Extract to a folder such as <1>C:\SteamCMD</1>.
step1.manualStep2Posix: Extract to a folder such as <1>~/steamcmd</1>.
step1.manualStep3: Run <1>steamcmd</1> once so it can self-update
step1.manualPathPlaceholder: Path to your existing SteamCMD folder
step1.downloadStalledStatus: Taking longer than expected -- SteamCMD may still be downloading. Reload this page to check its real status.

step2.title: Server Details
step2.description: Choose where files are installed and set the server identity.
step2.installFolderPlaceholder: Path to the dedicated server folder
step2.installFolderHelp: SteamCMD downloads about 3 GB of server files into this folder, creating it automatically if it doesn't exist yet — the panel just needs permission to write here. This is separate from where saves and settings are stored; see Custom config location below.
step2.linuxNoteBody1: If the panel runs through the bundled systemd service, use <1>{{path}}</1>. Other folders require a systemd permission change.
step2.linuxNoteBody2: The server data folder is created beside the install folder: <1>{{path}}</1>. Both folders must be writable.
step2.serverNameHelp: Alphanumeric characters and underscores only, e.g. myserver. This becomes the config file name (myserver.ini) — set it before installing. Changing it afterward creates a new, empty config instead of renaming the existing one.
step2.gameVersionHelp: Most people want Stable — it's the current default build. The other branches Steam offers here are older or experimental builds, kept around for compatibility with mods or saves that haven't updated yet. Saves and mods aren't guaranteed to work across different builds, so only switch if you specifically need one.
step2.customDataHelp: Leave this blank to create a data folder beside the install folder. In Docker, choose a bind-mounted folder when overriding it.

step3.title: Server Settings
step3.description: Configure remote control access and runtime options.
step3.rconDesc: This panel uses RCON to run commands on your server.

step4.title: Review and Install
step4.description: Confirm your settings, then begin the server download.
step4.portInfoIntro: Make sure your firewall or router allows:
step4.installingButton: Installing server... check the log below
step4.installStalledLog: This is taking longer than expected and the panel hasn't heard back from SteamCMD. The install may still be running in the background -- reload this page to check its real status before trying again.
step4.missingAdminPassword: Add an Admin Password in Advanced Options before installing.
step4.firstStartDesc: Start the server once to generate configuration files and world data. The first startup can take up to a minute.

quick.pageDescription: Create and register a server using existing dedicated server files.

step1.title: Select Server Files
step1.description: Choose the existing Project Zomboid dedicated server folder.
step1.usingExistingDesc: Select the existing Project Zomboid dedicated server folder, including its bundled Java runtime.
step1.usingExistingDescWindows: The folder should contain <1>StartServer64.bat</1> and the <3>java</3> folder.
step1.usingExistingDescPosix: The folder should contain <1>start-server.sh</1> and the <3>java</3> folder.
step1.locationPlaceholder: Path to your existing dedicated server folder
step1.locationHelp: Folder that already contains your Project Zomboid dedicated server files.

step2.title: Configure Server
step2.description: Set server name, RCON access, and memory limits.
step2.serverNameHelp: Alphanumeric characters and underscores only, e.g. myserver. Becomes the config file name (myserver.ini) for the existing server files you selected in the previous step.

step3.title: Review and Create
step3.description: Confirm these settings, then create your server entry.
step3.missingAdminPassword: Add an Admin Password in Advanced Options before creating the server.
